newsitem.title: USA: MGE wheat closes higher on exports, soy gains.
newsitem.headline: MGE wheat closes higher on exports, soy gains.

text.p: MGE spring wheat futures ended higher Thursday on strong export sales data and acreage switching ideas, MGE traders said.
"The beans are firm, and as long as they stay that way we'll probably be up," said one commission house trader.
Traders said that current high soybean prices and soggy ground in the Northern Plains will encourage wheat farmers to switch some acres from spring wheat to soybeans.
Analysts were looking for Monday's USDA prospective plantings report to show 18.55 million acres of spring wheat, which would be well below last year's tally of 20.04 million acres.
Higher-than-expected export sales also helped to fuel the moderate- to high-volume rally, MGE traders said.
The U.S. Department of Agriculture reported weekly export sales of 497,000 tonnes, which came in well above trade expectations for 100,000 to 300,000 tonnes.
Cargill was the session's best buyer in both the May and July contracts, pit traders said. Wilson Trading, Atwood and LFG were also buyers earlier in the session, traders said.
MGE spring wheat closed up 5-1/2 to 7-1/2 cents a bushel, with May up 5-1/2 at $4.18-1/2 and July up 5-3/4 at $4.09.
